name: Frances Acosta
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember earning a certificate while the best cook at home had none.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Frances by a small Tuesday habit. Frances checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I only hire qualified bakers. Watching this trial has made me wonder what my certificate never tested.
appearance: Frances has auburn hair cut square at the nape, a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, and a favorite piece of clothing, a boxy denim jacket. It usually goes with a pen clipped inside the neckline. When somebody else has the floor, Frances holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Frances is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Frances asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To let a capable unqualified baker into the next hiring round.
family: Remy Cruz is Frances’s second cousin. Frances brings the paper and a pen. Remy decides what stays off the paper. They have helped each other make decisions that were far easier to discuss once the figures could be moved around. The decisions themselves still belong to the person asking. Asked about *Names on the night wall*, Remy says, “I chose myself first. After a year of treatment, showing up each week really has been a shared decision between past and present me.”
connections: Edward Pike. The certificate holder and the blind taster disagree about where expertise is visible.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Frances asks which apartment is expecting someone home and makes sure that household knows about the delay.
